about: Every key of the 21 vendor Kannada keyboards (C:/Shree-Lipi nxt/*.KAN, loaded from their original paths) answered by S8KanU64.dll (TutorGetMappedCodeW, Unicode) and S8Kan764.dll (TutorGetMappedCode, Shree-Lipi 7 raw bytes; the 4/5/6 fonts SHREE-KAN-* draw the same bytes: fonts/family-check.json). Two capture runs (capvo/, capvo-b/) were byte-identical, and each run asked every key twice (#stable 1); every load verified in SLNXT's shared table (#loaded 1). layer 0 = printed keyboard (normal and shift are different ASCII keys), layer 1 = Ctrl+Space, layer 2 = the composer raw code layer (key char = internal code; NOT the Ctrl+Shift+1 symbol layer, which the tutor does not expose - see ctrlShift1). Per key: codes = the internal codes the key holds (a conjunct slot expanded, typed order), uHex/u = the Unicode composer answer raw / without its carrier, uRead = u in NFC, b7 = the 7 composer bytes. u null = no answer or a placeholder. Carriers to know: a lone vowel-sign key makes the 7 composer write the INDEPENDENT vowel glyph (ೆ -> 47 = ಎ), not a spelling; the lone reph key 4B makes the Unicode composer write ರ್ಕ (carrier ಕ) and the 7 composer the arkavattu glyph EC; the halant 44 and the link 64 alone: no 7 answer (garbage unit count).

ctrlShift1.source: the vendor charts (CHM "Special Keys", the same 13 keys in all 22 Kannada charts: assets/config/layouts/kan-*.json and kannada-inscript.json "symbols") + the composers' answers for the internal code of each character (single-code probes, capp/P-results.json). b7 null = the 7 composer types nothing for that code.
